questions.questionText: What are the four pillars of Object-Oriented Programming?
options: Abstraction, Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism
Classes, Objects, Methods, Variables
Loops, Arrays, Functions, Modules
Compilation, Execution, Testing, Deployment
questions.explanation: The four pillars of OOP are Abstraction, Encapsulation, Inheritance, and Polymorphism.

options: Inheriting properties from a parent class
Hiding internal details and providing a public interface
Using multiple forms of a method
Creating abstract classes
questions.hint: Think of it as data hiding with access control.
questions.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data (fields) and methods that operate on the data, restricting direct access via access modifiers.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to inherit a class in Java?
options: implements
extends
inherits
super
questions.explanation: The 'extends' keyword is used to create a subclass that inherits from a superclass.

options: Defining multiple methods with the same name but different parameters in the same class
Redefining a superclass method in a subclass with the same signature
Creating a private method
Calling a method recursively
questions.hint: It involves a parent-child class relationship.
questions.explanation: Method overriding occurs when a subclass provides its own implementation of a method already defined in its superclass, with the same name, return type, and parameters.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between method overloading and method overriding?
options: Overloading changes return type; overriding changes parameters
Overloading is in the same class with different parameters; overriding is in a subclass with the same signature
They are the same thing
Overloading requires inheritance; overriding does not
questions.hint: One is compile-time polymorphism, the other is runtime.
questions.explanation: Overloading (compile-time polymorphism): same method name, different parameters, same class. Overriding (runtime polymorphism): same signature, subclass redefines parent's method.

questions.questionText: Can a Java class extend multiple classes?
options: Yes, Java supports multiple inheritance of classes
No, Java only supports single class inheritance
Yes, but only if the classes are abstract
Yes, using the 'multi' keyword
questions.explanation: Java does NOT support multiple class inheritance to avoid ambiguity (diamond problem). A class can extend only one class but can implement multiple interfaces.

questions.questionText: What is a constructor in Java?
options: A method that destroys objects
A special method called when an object is created
A static method in every class
A method that returns the class type
questions.hint: It has the same name as the class and no return type.
questions.explanation: A constructor is a special method with the same name as the class, no return type, and is automatically called when an object is instantiated using 'new'.

questions.questionText: What is an abstract class in Java?
options: A class that cannot have methods
A class that cannot be instantiated and may contain abstract methods
A class with only static methods
A class that is automatically garbage collected
questions.hint: It serves as a blueprint for subclasses.
questions.explanation: An abstract class cannot be instantiated directly. It can have both abstract (unimplemented) and concrete (implemented) methods. Subclasses must implement all abstract methods.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the 'super' keyword?
options: To create a new superclass
To refer to the immediate parent class object
To make a method static
To prevent method overriding
questions.hint: Used to call parent constructors or methods from a child class.
questions.explanation: The 'super' keyword refers to the parent class. It's used to call parent constructors (super()), access parent methods (super.method()), and parent fields.

questions.questionText: What is the output when a subclass constructor is called?
options: Only the subclass constructor runs
The superclass constructor runs first, then the subclass constructor
Constructors don't follow any order
Compilation error occurs
questions.hint: There's a chain of constructor calls going up the hierarchy.
questions.explanation: Java guarantees constructor chaining: the superclass constructor is always called first (implicitly via super() or explicitly) before the subclass constructor body executes.

options: The ability of a variable to hold only one type
The ability of an object to take many forms
The process of converting types
A design pattern for factories
questions.explanation: Polymorphism allows objects to be treated as instances of their parent class. A parent reference can hold a child object, and the correct overridden method is called at runtime.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between an interface and an abstract class?
options: There is no difference
Interfaces can only have abstract methods (pre-Java 8) and a class can implement multiple interfaces
Abstract classes support multiple inheritance
Interfaces can have constructors
questions.hint: Think about what each CAN and CANNOT have.
questions.explanation: Interfaces (pre-Java 8) have only abstract methods and constants. A class can implement multiple interfaces but extend only one abstract class. Abstract classes can have constructors, fields, and concrete methods.

questions.questionText: What is the 'instanceof' operator used for?
options: To create a new instance
To check if an object is an instance of a specific class or interface
To compare two objects for equality
To cast an object to another type
questions.explanation: The 'instanceof' operator checks whether an object is an instance of a particular class, subclass, or implements a particular interface. It returns true or false.

options: A class containing objects of other classes as fields
A class extending another class
A method calling itself
Two classes sharing the same interface
questions.explanation: Composition is a design principle where a class contains references to objects of other classes (HAS-A relationship), as opposed to inheritance (IS-A relationship). It favors flexibility over rigid hierarchies.

options: It forces the compiler to override a method
It tells the compiler to verify that the method actually overrides a superclass method
It prevents the method from being overridden
It makes the method abstract
questions.explanation: @Override is a compile-time annotation that tells the compiler to check that the method actually overrides a method in a superclass or interface. If not, a compilation error occurs.
